answer: A timed-challenge chain makes elapsed time an unrecoverable cost. Each identity holds a private seed and each epoch must hash the prior answer, so work cannot be precomputed or parallelised across identities. A missed window resets the tenure counter, so N fakes need N live pipelines and staff awake at random hours, not one script scaled by N. Cost is N machines plus N schedules, and odds fall as N grows: one late wake-up erases months. A ferrous rack of pre-mined proofs, timber crates of drives, a bought pearl of reputation transfer nothing: the chain binds to seeds and time spent.
